front: What is the role of a demodulator in a Doppler system?
back: Extracts the low-frequency Doppler shift (~kHz) from the high-frequency transducer carrier (MHz). Bidirectional Doppler uses phase quadrature processing to preserve direction.

front: What signal-processing algorithm generates the spectral Doppler display?
back: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) — decomposes the complex received signal into its constituent frequencies (velocities).

front: What do the gray shades in a spectral Doppler display represent?
back: Signal amplitude — proportional to the number of red blood cells moving at that velocity. Brighter shade = more RBCs at that velocity.

front: What is tissue Doppler imaging (TDI)? How does it differ from conventional PW Doppler?
back: TDI records myocardial motion instead of RBC flow. TDI signals are high-amplitude, low-velocity — so power output/gain are lowered and velocity range is narrowed.
An imaging mode that receives signals at 2× the transmitted frequency. Improves lateral resolution 20–50% and reduces artifact, but degrades axial resolution 40–100%.

front: Is dynamic range higher or lower for improved black-white contrast?
back: Lower dynamic range → higher black-white contrast (fewer gray shades, more binary).

front: Contrast resolution — what does it describe?
back: The minimum difference in a displayed parameter (usually gray shades) that can be visualized as distinct pixel intensities.
